meta.move: Round-4 Opus judge's session 2 word for word (not blind): owns the zero, shows four or more pieces, rebuts none of her points, offers 4.4
meta.expect: No deal while none of her points has been answered

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Why did nobody call me before my son's mark changed?
Thanks for coming in. So, the AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94%, which is pretty conclusive, so that's why he got the zero.
A machine's guess. The company that sells it says it shouldn't be the only basis for punishing a student.

Let me back up, because I started in the wrong place. I entered the zero on November 3 before calling you. Your printed procedure, 4.2, says I should have called first. That was wrong, and Owen should not have found out on his phone in class.
Okay. What else do you have besides the score?

I'll set the checker aside; it's my weakest piece. I've turned my screen to you: this is the version history of Owen's essay. The document was created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM, with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. Then 23 minutes of small edits to font, name and spacing. No earlier drafts.
I'm writing those times down. Students draft in other documents and paste them in, so that proves nothing yet.

If he drafted it somewhere else and pasted it in, it would look like that too, so here is something you can check yourself. The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line is not in Hamlet. Here's the play open to 3.2. Look for it.
Slower. I'll read the scene myself. Okay. Is anything on his record right now?
And here is his outline from October 15, which he handed in himself. It argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues "epistemological paralysis" and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their argument between an outline and an essay. And you haven't answered me: is anything on his record today?

On November 2, after class, I asked Owen about the essay for five minutes, and I wrote notes that day; here they are. Asked what "epistemological paralysis" means, he said "like, being stuck." He couldn't say which scene his second paragraph was about. And here is his in-class writing from September 24: 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, comma splices throughout, no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine quotations cited by act, scene and line.
Notes you wrote yourself, about a seventeen-year-old put on the spot after class. The history and the quote are the pieces I can check. I want those on paper, dated, tonight.

I'm not asking you to say Owen cheated. Here's what I'm offering under procedure 4.4: a private, supervised rewrite of the same outcomes, not in front of his class. Its mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
Fine. For Owen's sake, to put this behind him, I'll accept a private rewrite. The zero comes off, nothing goes on his file, and I want it in writing tonight. Everything else I'll put in my email.
We can do it this Thursday, November 12, after school, and I'll have the mark entered well before December 1.
Thursday, the twelfth, after school. Okay. Put that date in the email with the rest.
Do we have an agreement?
Yes. A private rewrite on Thursday, the zero replaced by its mark, nothing on his record, all of it in writing tonight.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

We agreed that Owen will complete a private, supervised rewrite on Thursday, November 12, after school, that its mark will replace the zero, and that nothing will be placed on his record, under procedure 4.4. I still require the version history and the Hamlet quotation in writing with their dates, and a straight answer on whether anything is on his record today. I expect all of it in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and accepted a private supervised rewrite on Thursday, November 12, with its mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record, which is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4; she still wants your evidence on paper and an answer on whether anything is on his record now, and her time did not run out.
What moved her: You told her to check the quoted line in the play itself, because it was specific, tied to Owen's own essay and something she could verify without trusting you.
What cost ground: You opened with the detector score as conclusive, which handed her an easy point about a machine's guess and made you start by backing up.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the writing late on the night of October 28, starting at 11:31 PM, which came close to that night, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she first asked whether anything was on his record, answer it right then, because leaving it hanging while you stacked up more evidence let her keep control of the conversation.
